record.original_question: Let M be a closed manifold not covered by a sphere.

evidence.quote: Let M be a closed manifold not covered by a sphere.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is called a Besse manifold if every geodesic of $g$ is closed (the periods are not required to be equal). A compact rank one symmetric space (CROSS) is, by definition, one of the spaces $S^n$, $\mathbb{RP}^n$, $\mathbb{CP}^n$, $\mathbb{HP}^n$, or $\mathbb{OP}^2$ equipped with its standard symmetric Riemannian metric.

Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth manifold that is not covered by a sphere, and suppose $g$ is a smooth Riemannian metric on $M$ such that every geodesic of $g$ is closed. Prove or disprove: $(M,g)$ is, up to isometry (and up to a constant rescaling of $g$), one of the compact rank one symmetric spaces $\mathbb{RP}^n$, $\mathbb{CP}^n$, $\mathbb{HP}^n$, or $\mathbb{OP}^2$ endowed with its standard metric.
artifact.category_tag: Riemannian manifolds with all geodesics closed
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is a long-standing question in Riemannian geometry concerning the rigidity of Besse/P-manifolds (manifolds where all geodesics are closed) on bases that are not spheres. Although the Blaschke-type conjecture has been verified in some special cases (e.g., for $\mathbb{RP}^n$ with the additional Blaschke hypothesis), the general classification of Besse manifolds not covered by a sphere as CROSSes remains open and is repeatedly listed as an open problem in surveys on geodesics.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics (ar5iv)
status_evidence.snippet: Question 8.9.1: Let M be a closed manifold not covered by a sphere. Let g be a metric on M for which all geodesics are closed. Is (M,g) a CROSS (=compact rank one symmetric) manifold (with the standard metric)?
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as an open problem in the section on metrics with all geodesics closed.

status_evidence.title: Closed geodesic - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: The classification of manifolds all of whose geodesics are closed (Besse manifolds) is a long-standing open problem outside the case of the sphere.
status_evidence.claim: The general classification of Besse manifolds remains open.
